section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study that translated and adapted the CEMS and IES-2 scales into Brazilian Portuguese and examined their psychometric properties in a sample of Brazilian Portuguese-speaking adults. The study found that both scales demonstrated adequate factorial validity, discriminant validity, and reliability after minor modifications, and that the fitted models were invariant across sex (female and male samples). Key findings include significant negative correlations between restrictive/critical caregiver messages and body valorisation in both women and men, and weak correlations between intuitive eating factors and BMI, suggesting that caregiver messages and intuitive eating are only weakly associated with body weight.
